answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each identity to solve a unique sequential proof-of-work puzzle before joining: the puzzle cannot be parallelized, so one attacker running a thousand hollow shells still pays full compute per identity. Honest agents solve one puzzle once, but an attacker faces a steep ridge of cost that grows with every fake account. A saffron badge marks identities that completed the puzzle, letting peers trust newcomers cheaply while making mass forgery economically irrational.
